title: LLM Fundamentals
lede: A dense, citation-backed reference for ten topics every ML engineer, applied researcher, and platform builder needs to internalise — tokens, families, sampling, structured outputs, tool use, multimodal, embeddings, reasoning, and the trade-offs that decide which model runs in production. Each section ships in two voices: the engineer's version (technical, with code & diagrams) and a layman's version (plain English with analogies) at the bottom of each topic. প্রতিটি টপিকের শেষে বাংলা ব্যাখ্যাও আছে।

sections.title: Tokens, tokenization & context cost
sections.sub: Everything a model does — attention, generation, cost — is denominated in tokens, not characters or words. If your prompt shrinks from 800 to 200 tokens, you just cut cost by 75% and latency by a meaningful fraction. This is the single biggest engineering lever you have.

body.html: What is a token?

A token is one element in the model's vocabulary. Modern LLMs don't read characters; they read the output of a subword tokenizer — most commonly Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), which iteratively merges the most frequent adjacent pairs in a corpus until a target vocabulary size (often 32k–200k) is reached.[15] For multilingual and code workloads, SentencePiece is the dominant alternative — it operates directly on raw Unicode bytes or whitespace, treating language as a configuration parameter.[16]

body.html: Why this matters: the cost equation

APIs charge per token, not per character. A useful mnemonic: ~1 token ≈ 4 characters in English for most modern tokenizers, but this varies wildly by language — Chinese runs ~1 char ≈ 1.5 tokens, code ~1 token ≈ 3.5 chars, numbers are split digit-by-digit in early tokenizers but consolidated in newer ones.

# Counting tokens with tiktoken (OpenAI) or transformers
import tiktoken
enc = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("gpt-4o")
text = "Tokenization is the silent tax on every LLM call."
print(len(enc.encode(text)))   # → 11 tokens, not 8 words

# Concrete cost (input, gpt-4o-mini, Jul 2025 pricing)
tokens        = 11
price_per_m   = 0.15      # USD per 1M input tokens
cost_per_call = tokens / 1_000_000 * price_per_m   # → $0.00000165

Context windows — what they actually are

The context window is the maximum total tokens (input + output) the model can attend to in a single call. It has grown dramatically: GPT-3's 2K window in 2020 → 8K (GPT-3.5) → 128K (GPT-4o) → 1M+ (Gemini 1.5).[1][11]

blocks.html: Long context ≠ free performance. Even with 1M-token windows, retrieval-augmented generation, summarisation, or hierarchical attention beats dumping 800K tokens in. Needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks improve, but multi-hop reasoning across long contexts degrades sharply. Measure on your own workloads.

body.html: How tokens map to cost & latency

rows: Quadratic attention compute; ~100 ms–2 s on modern APIs for 10K tokens
Sequential (one per step); output tokens are 3–5× more expensive than input on most APIs
Prompt caching (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) cuts repeated-prefix cost by ~80–90%
A 1M-token call isn't 125× a 8K call — closer to 5–8× due to attention scaling and chunked prefill

layman.html: Think of a token like a "word piece." When you read this sentence, you see whole words. An LLM doesn't see words — it sees chunks. "Unbelievable" might be three chunks: un + believ + able. Common chunks like "the" or "ing" are single chunks. Weird stuff ("Doha", "kubernetes") gets chopped into more chunks.

Why does this matter to you? Because every API charge is per chunk, not per word. A 100-word email is roughly 130 chunks. A 100-word email stuffed with code and rare names might be 220 chunks. Same email, double the cost — just from language alone.

Context window = the model's short-term memory. You know how if a friend has been listening for 4 hours straight, they start forgetting things you said an hour ago? LLMs do the same thing, just more abruptly. "Context window" is the size of their working memory — usually 8K to 1M chunks. Bigger isn't always better: cramming 800K chunks in doesn't make the model 100× smarter, it just makes the bill bigger.

blocks.html: The kitchen analogy: tokens are like "ingredients on the counter." The context window is the counter size. A tiny counter (2K) means you can only cook small meals. A huge counter (1M) lets you cook for a wedding — but you still have to actually cook, and the bigger meal doesn't come out better just because you had room.

bangla.html: Token হলো LLM-এর ভোকাবুলারির একেকটি টুকরো। মডেল অক্ষর বা পুরো শব্দ পড়ে না; একটি subword tokenizer শব্দকে ভেঙে ছোট ছোট অংশে পরিণত করে, যার জনপ্রিয় পদ্ধতি BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding)। এটি corpus-এর সবচেয়ে ঘন ঘন পাশাপাশি আসা জোড়াগুলো বারবার মিলিয়ে নেয়, যতক্ষণ না নির্দিষ্ট vocabulary size (প্রায়ই 32k–200k) হয়। বহুভাষিক ও কোডের কাজে SentencePiece বেশি ব্যবহৃত হয়। মডেল শেষ পর্যন্ত শুধু token ID (পূর্ণসংখ্যা) দেখে, যা embedding table-এ যায়।

খরচের হিসাব হয় token দিয়ে, অক্ষর দিয়ে নয়। ইংরেজিতে মোটামুটি 1 token ≈ 4 অক্ষর, কিন্তু ভাষাভেদে এটি অনেক বদলায়: চীনা ভাষায় 1 অক্ষর ≈ 1.5 token, কোডে 1 token ≈ 3.5 অক্ষর। তাই prompt 800 থেকে 200 token-এ নামালে খরচ 75% কমে এবং latency-ও কমে। এটাই সবচেয়ে বড় engineering lever।

Context window হলো এক কলে মডেল সর্বোচ্চ কত token (input + output মিলিয়ে) দেখতে পারে। এটি GPT-3-এর 2K থেকে বেড়ে এখন 1M+ পর্যন্ত গেছে। খরচ ও গতির দিক থেকে: prefill (prompt প্রসেসিং) এর খরচ input token অনুযায়ী, আর decode (লেখা তৈরি) ধাপে ধাপে হয় এবং output token সাধারণত input-এর চেয়ে 3–5 গুণ দামি। Prompt caching বারবার আসা prefix-এর খরচ প্রায় 80–90% কমায়।

সতর্কতা: বড় context মানে নিখুঁত পারফরম্যান্স নয়। 800K token ঢেলে দেওয়ার চেয়ে RAG বা summarisation প্রায়ই ভালো, কারণ লম্বা context-এ multi-hop reasoning দ্রুত খারাপ হয়। নিজের workload-এ মেপে দেখুন।

blocks.html: দর্জির দোকানের উপমা: কাপড়ের থান (পুরো লেখা) দর্জি আগে ছোট ছোট টুকরোয় কেটে নেয় (token), আর মজুরি হয় টুকরোর সংখ্যা ধরে। Context window হলো দর্জির কাটিং টেবিলের মাপ: টেবিল যত বড়, একসাথে তত কাপড় ছড়িয়ে কাজ করা যায়। কিন্তু টেবিল বড় হলেই জামা সুন্দর হয় না; আর অকারণে বেশি কাপড় ছড়ালে খরচ ও সময় দুটোই বাড়ে।

practice.title: Cut prompt tokens, keep the answer
practice.goal: See that a shorter prompt gives the same answer, then count how much money fewer tokens save.
steps: Send Prompt A in a new chat. Note the answer.
Send Prompt B in another new chat. Compare the answer and the length of the two prompts.
Send Prompt C in the same chat as Prompt B. Check the maths yourself with a calculator.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
Hello! I hope you are having a wonderful day. I am working on a customer support system and I would really appreciate your kind help with a small task. Below you will find a customer ticket. Could you please read the ticket very carefully and then tell me which one of the following categories it belongs to? The categories are: billing, shipping, defect, account. Please choose only one category. When you answer, please do not write any explanation, any greeting, or any extra sentence. Just write the single category word. Thank you so much for your help!

Ticket: My order #48213 arrived yesterday and the screen is cracked. I want my money back.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
Classify the ticket as one of: billing, shipping, defect, account. Reply with the category only.

Ticket: My order #48213 arrived yesterday and the screen is cracked. I want my money back.

prompts.label: Prompt C
prompts.text: A support bot sends 800 input tokens per call. A shorter prompt sends 200 input tokens per call. The price is $0.50 per 1 million input tokens. The bot makes 2 million calls per month. Calculate the monthly input cost for each prompt, and the percentage saved. Show each step.

lookFor: Both chats usually give the same one-word answer, even though Prompt A is about four times longer.
Every extra word in Prompt A is extra tokens, and you pay for every one of them on every call.
Prompt C gives about $800 for the long prompt and $200 for the short one: a 75% saving.

check.question: Why does the length of a prompt matter for cost, if the answer stays the same?
check.answer: APIs charge per token, and the model reads every input token on every call. A prompt with 75% fewer tokens costs 75% less in input cost and has less prefill work, so it also responds faster.

practice.challenge: Shorten Prompt B even more, without changing the answer. Then try a prompt in another language, such as Bengali, and ask if it is likely to use more tokens for the same meaning.

body.html: Architectural distinctions that matter

blocks.html: Every parameter is used on every token. Predictable compute, simple serving. Examples: Llama 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B.[2][4]

Routes each token to a subset of "expert" FFNs. Total params large but active params per token small → cheaper inference, larger memory. Mixtral 8×7B, DeepSeek-V3 (671B/37B active), Qwen3-235B-A22B.[5][6][28]
DeepSeek's innovation: compresses the KV cache into a low-rank latent, slashing memory for long contexts.[6]
Mistral 7B pioneered sliding-window attention for cheap inference. Gemini 1.5 mixes local + global attention for million-token contexts.[4][11]

layman.html: Imagine cars on a road. Each "model family" is a different car brand — they all get you from A to B, but they have different personalities. Anthropic (Claude) is the careful Volvo: best at reading long, complicated documents and being safe. OpenAI (GPT) is the polished Tesla: the most famous, with a huge ecosystem of accessories. Google (Gemini) is the minivan: huge cargo space (it can hold millions of words at once) and built-in cameras. Meta (Llama) is the kit car: you get the blueprints for free and build it yourself in your garage. Mistral is the European hatchback — small, nimble, made in France.

And then there are the Chinese manufacturers. Alibaba's Qwen and DeepSeek are like Xiaomi and BYD: they came out of nowhere, the open-weights version is free, and benchmarks say they keep up with the expensive brands. In 2024–2025 they went from "who?" to "frontier-tier."

Why are some free? "Open-weight" means the company released the file containing the model's brain — anyone can download it. They still trained it on expensive computers, but once the file exists, copying it costs nothing. It's the difference between a chef who sells them dishes (closed) and a chef who publishes the recipe (open).

Which should you pick? If you're a regular user, just use the brand with the best app (probably ChatGPT or Claude). If you're building software: pick closed for the absolute best capability, pick open-weight to save money at scale or keep it inside your company.

blocks.html: The car analogy again: closed models = renting a luxury car monthly. Open-weight = buying the car (or a cheap one) outright. If you drive 100 miles a month, renting is cheap. If you drive 100,000, buying wins. The 2025 sweet spot for most companies: rent for hard problems, own for the easy stuff you do millions of times.

bangla.html: "সেরা মডেল" বলে কিছু নেই, প্রশ্ন হলো আপনার workload-এর জন্য কোন trade-off মানানসই। প্রধান পরিবারগুলো: OpenAI (GPT-4o, o3, GPT-5) reasoning ও পরিণত ecosystem-এ ভালো; Anthropic (Claude 4) লম্বা context (200K), কোড-এজেন্ট ও দীর্ঘ ডকুমেন্ট বিশ্লেষণে ভালো; Google (Gemini 2.5) native multimodal ও 1–2M context-এ এগিয়ে; Meta (Llama 3.1) open weights ও শক্তিশালী ছোট মডেল; Mistral ইউরোপীয় data residency ও edge deployment-এর জন্য; Alibaba Qwen3 সস্তা self-host ও বহুভাষিক কাজে; DeepSeek (V3, R1) কম training খরচে শক্তিশালী open-weight reasoning-এ।

স্থাপত্যগত পার্থক্যও গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। Dense transformer-এ প্রতিটি token-এর জন্য সব parameter ব্যবহার হয়, তাই compute অনুমানযোগ্য ও serving সহজ। Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-এ প্রতিটি token শুধু কিছু "expert" FFN-এ যায়: মোট parameter বিশাল কিন্তু active parameter কম, ফলে inference সস্তা হলেও memory বেশি লাগে (যেমন DeepSeek-V3: 671B মোট, 37B active)। MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) KV cache-কে ছোট করে লম্বা context-এর memory বাঁচায়। Sliding-window বা hybrid attention সস্তা inference ও বিশাল context-এ সাহায্য করে।
বাছাইয়ের নিয়ম: সর্বোচ্চ ক্ষমতা লাগলে closed মডেল, আর খরচ কমানো বা data নিজেদের কাছে রাখতে চাইলে open-weight।

blocks.html: পরিবহনের উপমা: প্রতিদিন অফিস করতে আপনি কখনো রিকশা, কখনো বাস, আবার জরুরি দরকারে উবার নেন। সব যানই গন্তব্যে পৌঁছে দেয়, কিন্তু দাম, আরাম ও গতি আলাদা। তেমনি সহজ কাজ ছোট সস্তা মডেলে, আর কঠিন কাজ ফ্রন্টিয়ার মডেলে চালানোই বুদ্ধিমানের কাজ।

practice.title: Match a model to the workload
practice.goal: Practise choosing a model by trade-off, not by the word best, and see why a MoE model needs more memory.
steps: Read the three workloads in Prompt A. Before you send it, write your own choice of model for each.
Send Prompt A in a new chat. Compare the AI choices with yours. Note any difference.
Send Prompt B in the same chat. Compare its answer with your first guess.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
I must pick one model for each workload. The three models are made-up.

Model X: large, very strong at reasoning, slow, expensive per token, closed API.
Model Y: small, fast, cheap per token, good at simple tasks, closed API.
Model Z: medium, open weights, you run it on your own servers, you must pay for GPUs and operations.

Workloads:
1. A chat helper that sorts 5 million short support tickets per month into 4 categories.
2. A coding agent that fixes hard bugs across many files. Only 200 tasks per day.
3. A hospital in a country where patient data must never leave the building. Medium difficulty questions.

For each workload, choose X, Y or Z. Give one sentence on the trade-off. Then say why 'which model is the best' is the wrong question.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text: A Mixture-of-Experts model has 671B total parameters but only 37B active per token. A dense model has 70B parameters, and all of them are active on every token. Which model needs more GPU memory to load? Which model does less computing per token? Answer in 3 short sentences.

lookFor: Most models pick Y for the high-volume tickets, X for the hard coding tasks, and Z for the data-residency case.
The AI usually names a different trade-off for each workload: cost, capability, or data control.
For Prompt B, the MoE model needs more memory, but does less computing per token.

check.question: Why does a MoE model use more memory than a 70B dense model but less compute per token?
check.answer: All experts must be loaded in memory, so the total parameters decide the memory. Each token is routed to only a few experts, so only the active parameters do the compute.

practice.challenge: Change workload 1 to only 500 tickets per month. Ask the AI if the choice changes, and why.

sections.title: Closed vs open-weight models
sections.sub: "Open" splits into two camps that engineers often confuse: open-weight (you can download and run the model) and open-source (you also have training code, data, and licence to modify and redistribute). Most "open" LLMs are open-weight.

body.html: Closed / proprietary

Hosted behind APIs. Examples: GPT-4o/o3/GPT-5, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5. Advantages: highest capability ceiling, fastest hardware optimisation, integrated safety stack, no infra to run. Costs: vendor lock-in, no auditability of weights, data leaves your perimeter, price changes are unilateral.[14][13]
Open-weight

Weights released under a licence (often Apache 2.0, Llama Community License, or MIT). Examples: Llama 3.1 (8B–405B),[3] Mistral 7B & Mixtral 8×7B,[4][5] Qwen2.5/Qwen3,[8][9] DeepSeek-V3 / R1.[6][7] Advantages: self-host on your hardware, fine-tune on private data, audit weights, no per-token fees, no data egress. Costs: you operate the infra (GPUs, networking, monitoring), capability ceiling ~3–9 months behind the frontier, safety is your problem.

blocks.html: When open-weight wins: predictable cost at scale, data residency / compliance requirements, need to fine-tune on proprietary data, latency-sensitive serving where inference co-locates with state.

When closed wins: tasks where you're 3–9 months behind the SOTA matters (frontier coding agents, reasoning), small query volume makes self-hosting uneconomical, you need multimodal audio/video (Gemini).

body.html: Hybrid patterns becoming standard

items: Distillation: DeepSeek-R1's distilled Qwen/Llama variants prove you can train strong small open models from a closed teacher's outputs.[7]
Routing: route easy queries to a local 8B, hard ones to a frontier API. Saves cost without measurable quality loss on common tasks.
Open-weights with closed APIs: Llama 3.1 405B is open, and you can also call it via Together, Groq, Fireworks for managed serving — keeping the option to migrate.

layman.html: "Closed" vs "open-weight" is about who owns the brain.

Closed (GPT, Claude, Gemini): the AI lives on the company's servers. You talk to it through their app or API. Your data travels to them, they run the model, the answer travels back. You can never inspect the actual model — like renting a black-box appliance.

Open-weight (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral): the company released the file containing all the model's "knowledge" — billions of numbers that together form a brain. Anyone can download this file (it's huge — 8 to 700 gigabytes) and run it on their own computers. The recipe is public, even if the cookbook is not.

What's the catch? "Open-weight" is not the same as "open-source." You usually can't see how it was trained, what data, or modify it freely. You can run it, fine-tune it on your own data, and deploy it. But retraining from scratch? That costs millions of dollars in computers.

The 2025 reality: open-weight models got so good that for most business tasks, a free open-weight model running on rented GPUs is 80% as good as GPT-4 at 10% of the cost. Companies are quietly switching. The frontier closed models (Claude 4, GPT-5) still lead on hard reasoning, but the gap is small.

blocks.html: The cookbook analogy: closed = a chef who sells you meals but won't share recipes. Open-weight = a chef who wrote the recipe book; you can cook it yourself or pay someone to cook it for you. Open-source = a chef who shared the kitchen, the suppliers, AND the recipes — that's almost never available for LLMs.

bangla.html: "Open" শব্দটি দুই অর্থে ব্যবহৃত হয় এবং ইঞ্জিনিয়াররা প্রায়ই গুলিয়ে ফেলেন। Open-weight মানে মডেলের weights ডাউনলোড করে নিজে চালানো যায়। Open-source মানে এর সাথে training code, data এবং পরিবর্তন ও পুনর্বিতরণের লাইসেন্সও পাওয়া যায়। বেশিরভাগ "open" LLM আসলে শুধু open-weight।

Closed/proprietary মডেল (GPT, Claude, Gemini) API-র পেছনে থাকে। সুবিধা: সর্বোচ্চ ক্ষমতা, দ্রুত hardware optimisation, তৈরি safety stack, নিজের infra চালাতে হয় না। অসুবিধা: vendor lock-in, weights যাচাই করা যায় না, data আপনার সীমানার বাইরে যায়, আর দাম তারা একতরফা বদলাতে পারে।

Open-weight (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) মডেলে আপনি নিজের হার্ডওয়্যারে চালাতে পারেন, private data-য় fine-tune করতে পারেন, weights audit করতে পারেন, per-token ফি লাগে না এবং data বাইরে যায় না। বিনিময়ে GPU, networking ও monitoring আপনাকেই চালাতে হবে, ক্ষমতা ফ্রন্টিয়ার থেকে প্রায় 3–9 মাস পিছিয়ে, আর safety-র দায়ও আপনার।

items: Open-weight জেতে যখন scale-এ অনুমানযোগ্য খরচ, data residency/compliance, proprietary data-য় fine-tuning বা latency-সংবেদী serving দরকার।
Closed জেতে যখন ফ্রন্টিয়ার কোডিং/reasoning লাগে, query কম বলে self-host লাভজনক নয়, অথবা audio/video multimodal দরকার।
Hybrid প্যাটার্ন এখন সাধারণ: distillation, সহজ query ছোট লোকাল মডেলে ও কঠিনগুলো ফ্রন্টিয়ার API-তে পাঠানো (routing), এবং Together/Groq/Fireworks-এর মতো managed serving।

blocks.html: বাসা ভাড়া বনাম নিজের বাড়ির উপমা: Closed মডেল ভাড়া বাসার মতো: মালিক সব দেখভাল করে, কিন্তু ভাড়া বাড়ালে আপনার কিছু করার নেই, আর দেয়াল ভাঙার অনুমতি নেই। Open-weight হলো নিজের বাড়ি: ইচ্ছেমতো সাজাতে পারেন, কিন্তু মেরামত ও পাহারার ঝামেলা আপনার। আর Open-source হলো বাড়ির নকশা, ইট-সিমেন্টের হিসাব ও কারিগর সবকিছু পাওয়া, যা LLM-এর ক্ষেত্রে প্রায় দেখাই যায় না।

practice.title: Find the break-even for self-hosting
practice.goal: Work out when an open-weight model on your own GPU is cheaper than a closed API, and when it is not.
steps: Send Prompt A in a new chat. Check the break-even number with a calculator.
Send Prompt B in the same chat. Write your own choice for each company first.
Compare your choices with the AI choices. Find one case where you disagree and decide who is right.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
Compare two options for the same text task.

Option 1, closed API: $3 per 1 million tokens (input and output mixed). No other cost.
Option 2, open-weight model on our own server: $2,200 per month for the GPU server plus $1,500 per month for engineer time. It can serve up to 2 billion tokens per month. No per-token fee.

At how many tokens per month do both options cost the same? Show the formula and the steps. Which option is cheaper at 200 million tokens per month? Which at 1.8 billion?

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
For each company below, choose: closed API, open-weight self-host, or hybrid (route easy queries to a small local model, hard queries to a frontier API). Give one sentence of reason each.

Company 1: A small start-up with 50,000 queries per month, no ML engineers.
Company 2: A bank that must keep all customer text inside its own data centre. It also has a team that can run GPUs.
Company 3: A shopping app with 100 million queries per month. 80% are simple, and 20% need top quality.
Company 4: A team that must use the strongest coding agent available today.

lookFor: The break-even is about 1.23 billion tokens per month: ($2,200 + $1,500) divided by $3 per million.
At 200 million tokens the API is far cheaper. At 1.8 billion tokens self-hosting is cheaper.
Most models pick closed for company 1 and 4, open-weight for company 2, and hybrid for company 3.

check.question: Why can a closed API be cheaper for a small team even if open-weight models have no per-token fee?
check.answer: With open weights you pay a fixed cost for GPUs and operations, whatever the volume. At low volume that fixed cost is spread over few tokens, so the per-token API price is lower. Open-weight wins when volume, data residency, or fine-tuning needs are high.

practice.challenge: Ask Prompt A again with a server that costs $6,000 per month and handles 5 billion tokens. Where is the new break-even, and is it still inside the server capacity?

sections.sub: A model outputs a probability distribution over every token in its vocabulary. Sampling is how you turn that distribution into text. The same logits can produce robotic lists, creative prose, or factual hallucinations depending on five knobs.

k=1 = greedy. k≈40–100 typical. Avoid k<10 with high temperature.

)

blocks.html: Don't combine top_k and top_p aggressively. Either pick top_k (fixed vocabulary cut) or top_p (probability mass cut). Using both with tight values double-strips the tail and can cause degeneration. Modern providers recommend temperature + top_p (or temperature + min_p), full stop.

layman.html: Inside the AI, every word is a dice roll. When the model writes "The cat sat on the..." it has a list of probabilities: mat 40%, floor 25%, couch 15%, roof 8%, ... and thousands of weird options at fractions of a percent. The model has to choose one. How it chooses is "sampling."

Temperature is the dice's "creativity dial." Set it to 0 and the model always picks mat — boring, predictable, perfect for code or facts. Crank it up to 1.2 and it might pick roof, cathedral, or porcupine — fun, surprising, occasionally nonsense. Set it to 2 and it's babbling.

top_p and top_k are "filters." Imagine you only let the dice roll the top 50 candidates (top_k=50), or only the candidates whose probabilities add up to 90% (top_p=0.9). This stops it from picking the bizarre long-shots.
Penalties are memory aids. "frequency_penalty" means "stop saying the the the the the." "presence_penalty" means "you already mentioned dogs, try a new topic."
The cheat sheet: code/JSON/facts → temperature 0. Chat → 0.7. Creative writing → 1.0–1.3. Don't combine lots of filters — pick one and trust it.

blocks.html: The dinner party analogy: the model is a friend picking from the menu. Temperature 0 = "always order the safest thing." Temperature 1 = "pick whatever sounds good tonight." Temperature 2 = "order whatever's weirdest on the menu." top_p/top_k = "don't even look at the last 3 pages of the menu, nothing weird there is worth trying."

bangla.html: মডেল প্রতিটি ধাপে ভোকাবুলারির সব token-এর ওপর একটি সম্ভাবনা বণ্টন (probability distribution) তৈরি করে। Sampling হলো সেই বণ্টন থেকে একটি token বেছে নেওয়ার পদ্ধতি। একই logits থেকে এই knob-গুলোর কারণে কখনো রোবটিক তালিকা, কখনো সৃজনশীল লেখা বা hallucination বেরোতে পারে।

items: temperature: softmax-এর আগে logits-কে T দিয়ে ভাগ করে। T<1 হলে বণ্টন ধারালো (বেশি deterministic), T>1 হলে সমতল (বেশি random)। কোড, JSON, classification, math-এর জন্য 0; chat-এর জন্য 0.7–1.0; সৃজনশীল লেখা ও brainstorming-এর জন্য 1.0–2.0।
top_k: শুধু সবচেয়ে সম্ভাব্য k-টি token থেকে বাছে। k=1 মানে greedy; সাধারণত k≈40–100। বেশি temperature-এর সাথে k<10 এড়ানো ভালো।
top_p (nucleus): যে ক্ষুদ্রতম token-সেটের সম্মিলিত সম্ভাবনা ≥ p, শুধু সেটি রাখে। সাধারণত 0.9–0.95।
min_p: top token-এর সম্ভাবনার min_p গুণের চেয়ে কম সম্ভাবনার token বাদ দেয়; মডেলের আকার বদলালেও এটি ভালো কাজ করে।
frequency_penalty: token যতবার এসেছে তার সংখ্যা অনুযায়ী logit কমায়, ফলে পুনরাবৃত্তি কমে (সাধারণত 0.1–1.0)।
presence_penalty: token একবার এসে থাকলেই কমায়, ফলে বিষয়ের বৈচিত্র্য বাড়ে (সাধারণত 0–0.6)।

bangla.html: সাধারণ ভুল: top_k ও top_p একসাথে কড়াভাবে দিলে tail দুইবার ছাঁটা হয়ে লেখা অসংলগ্ন (degeneration) হতে পারে। আধুনিক প্রোভাইডাররা temperature + top_p (অথবা temperature + min_p) ব্যবহারের পরামর্শ দেন।

blocks.html: চায়ের দোকানের উপমা: আপনি চায়ের দোকানে গেছেন। Temperature 0 হলো রোজকার মতো সেই একই নিরাপদ চা অর্ডার করা। Temperature বাড়ালে আপনি নতুন কিছু চেখে দেখার ঝুঁকি নেন, আর খুব বেশি হলে যা-তা অর্ডার করে বসেন। top_p/top_k হলো আগেই ঠিক করা: মেনুর শেষের পাতার অদ্ভুত আইটেমগুলো দেখবই না।

practice.title: See a sharp and a flat distribution
practice.goal: See that a model has a probability for many next words: sharp for facts, flat for creative text, and that sampling picks from them.
steps: Send Prompt A in a new chat. Then send Prompt B in the same chat. Compare the two probability lists.
Send Prompt C in three new chats. Write down the three words.
Compare: which prompt has one dominant word, and which has many close words?

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
Estimate the next-word probabilities for this sentence start. List the 5 most likely next words, each with a percentage. The percentages must add up to about 100%. Reply with the list only.

The capital of France is

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
Estimate the next-word probabilities for this sentence start. List the 5 most likely next words, each with a percentage. The percentages must add up to about 100%. Reply with the list only.

Once upon a time, there was a little

prompts.label: Prompt C
prompts.text:
Complete this sentence with one word only. Reply with the word and nothing else.

Once upon a time, there was a little

lookFor: For Prompt A, one word (Paris) usually has almost all of the probability.
For Prompt B, the percentages are spread over several words, such as girl, boy, fox, or rabbit.
In the three chats of Prompt C, the word often changes. The AI's percentages are its own estimate, not the real logits.

check.question: If the model always picked the single most likely word, what would change for Prompt C?
check.answer: It would give the same word every time. This is greedy decoding, like temperature near 0 or top_k=1. Sampling picks from the whole distribution, so a flat distribution gives different words, and a higher temperature flattens it more.

practice.challenge: Ask for the same list for the sentence start 2 + 2 equals. Is it sharper than Prompt A or flatter than Prompt B? Why?

sections.title: Streaming vs non-streaming
sections.sub: Generation is sequential — tokens come one at a time. Streaming returns them as they're produced via Server-Sent Events or chunked HTTP, so the UI can render the first word while the rest is still being decoded. Non-streaming waits for the full response.

body.html: Trade-offs

items: Any user-facing chat / completion UI
Long generations where the user needs feedback that the model is "thinking"
Tools like Cursor, Claude.ai, ChatGPT — every product is streaming by default now
You're feeding output back into a pipeline (function-call result, structured extractor)
You need the full response for JSON parsing / validation
Batch jobs with no UX

layman.html: Without streaming, asking the AI a question is like waiting for a fax. You hit send, then wait in silence for 5–20 seconds, then the entire answer appears at once. With streaming, the answer appears word by word as the AI thinks of it — like a live chat bubble that fills in real time.

Is the AI faster? No, exactly the same. But it FEELS way faster. Reading the first word after 0.3 seconds (streaming) feels snappy. Waiting 8 seconds in silence for the whole answer (non-streaming) feels broken. Same total work, completely different vibe.

When should you turn streaming off? When the AI's answer isn't for humans to read directly. If you're piping the output into a database, or a code function, or a JSON parser, you want the whole answer validated before doing anything.
Every chat app you've used (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) streams by default. That's why the responses feel instant even though complex ones take 10+ seconds to compute.

blocks.html: The TV analogy: non-streaming = the network holds the whole show hostage and dumps it on your screen all at once. Streaming = watching it unfold live, second by second. Same show, totally different feeling.

bangla.html: LLM একটি একটি করে token তৈরি করে, অর্থাৎ generation ক্রমিক। Streaming-এ token তৈরি হওয়ার সাথে সাথে Server-Sent Events বা chunked HTTP দিয়ে পাঠানো হয়, ফলে বাকি অংশ তৈরি হওয়ার আগেই UI-তে প্রথম শব্দ দেখা যায়। Non-streaming-এ পুরো উত্তর তৈরি হওয়া পর্যন্ত অপেক্ষা করতে হয়।
মূল কথা: compute একই, কিন্তু perceived latency "সব-অথবা-কিছুই-না" থেকে ক্রমবর্ধমান হয়ে যায়, ফলে UX অনেক ভালো লাগে।

items: Streaming ব্যবহার করুন: ব্যবহারকারীর সামনে থাকা chat/completion UI-তে, লম্বা generation-এ যেখানে ব্যবহারকারীর জানা দরকার মডেল কাজ করছে, এবং Cursor, Claude.ai, ChatGPT-র মতো প্রোডাক্টে।
Streaming বাদ দিন: যখন আউটপুট pipeline-এ ফিরে যাচ্ছে (function-call result, structured extractor), পুরো response লাগে JSON parsing/validation-এর জন্য, অথবা UX-বিহীন batch job।

bangla.html: OpenAI SDK-তে stream=True দিয়ে প্রতিটি chunk-এর delta পড়তে হয়; Anthropic-এ client.messages.stream(...) থেকে text_stream পড়া যায়।

blocks.html: ক্রিকেট ম্যাচের উপমা: Non-streaming হলো খেলা শেষ হওয়ার পর শুধু চূড়ান্ত স্কোর জানা। Streaming হলো বল বাই বল লাইভ কমেন্ট্রি শোনা। খেলার সময় একই, কিন্তু অপেক্ষাটা অনেক সহনীয় লাগে।

practice.title: Time the first word and the last
practice.goal: Measure that streaming shows the first word fast while the full answer takes the same total time, and see why partial output is a problem for pipelines.
steps: Start a stopwatch as you send Prompt A in a new chat. Note the time of the first word and of the last word.
Send Prompt B in a new chat. Note the time to the full answer.
Send Prompt C in a new chat. Press Stop after about two seconds, if a Stop button shows. Read the partial text.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text: Write a story of about 400 words about a rickshaw driver in Dhaka who finds a lost umbrella during the monsoon.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text: Reply with only the word OK.

prompts.label: Prompt C
prompts.text: Return only a JSON object, with no other text and no code fence. The object has these fields: id, name, email, city, plan, signup_date, last_login, tags (an array of 5 strings), and notes (a 2 sentence string). Use made-up values.

lookFor: For Prompt A, the first words appear after a short wait, and the rest comes word by word. The total time is long.
Prompt B is so short that the first word and the full answer arrive at almost the same time.
The partial text from Prompt C is not valid JSON: the closing brace is missing, so a program could not parse it yet.

check.question: Why is streaming good for a chat window but often bad for a step in a data pipeline?
check.answer: Streaming does not make generation faster. It shows tokens as they arrive, so the user sees progress sooner. A pipeline step that must parse or validate JSON needs the complete response, so it should wait for the non-streaming result.

practice.challenge: Ask for a 1,000 word story. Does the time to the first word change much, compared with the 400 word story? What does this tell you about perceived latency?

sections.title: Structured outputs & JSON mode
sections.sub: Forcing free-form text into a typed schema unlocks LLMs as reliable components in larger pipelines. There are three progressively stricter approaches.

body.html: Schema-constrained generation: how it actually works

The provider compiles the schema into a finite-state machine (or grammar) and, at each generation step, masks the logits of any token that would violate the schema. Output is guaranteed to be parseable by construction — no defensive try/except needed.[26]

body.code:
# OpenAI Structured Outputs (Python)
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI

class Person(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int
    role: str

client = OpenAI()
resp = client.beta.chat.completions.parse(
    model="gpt-4o-2024-08-09",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Extract: Ada Lovelace, 36, mathematician"}],
    response_format=Person,
)
person: Person = resp.choices[0].message.parsed
print(person.name, person.age)    # typed, valid by construction

print(person.name, person.age)    # typed, valid by construction

blocks.html: Use structured outputs whenever you can. They turn LLM calls into well-typed function calls — no regex, no eval, no retry loops. The slight latency bump from FSM lookup is dwarfed by the saved post-validation.

layman.html: Imagine hiring a brilliant but very chatty assistant. You say "find me flights to London next Tuesday under $500" and they reply with a beautiful paragraph of text: "Certainly! I've looked up some lovely options, you might consider a British Airways departure at..." Now your software has to parse English to get the structured flight info. That's brittle and fails constantly.

Structured outputs fix this. Instead of free-form prose, the AI returns a perfectly-formatted package — like a shipping label. You said "give me {departure_city, arrival_city, date, price}" and you get exactly that, in JSON, every time. No parsing, no guessing, no surprise.
Three flavors:

• JSON mode — "respond with JSON" in the prompt. ~90% reliable, sometimes the shape drifts.
• Schema-constrained — you pass a strict shape; the AI physically cannot output anything that doesn't fit. ~99.9% reliable.
• Typed parsing — the schema-constrained output goes directly into a typed object in your code (Pydantic, Zod). 100% guaranteed.
Real impact: structured outputs turn "AI chat" into "AI as API." You can now build reliable software on top of LLMs because they return predictable data structures, not essays.

blocks.html: The form analogy: free-form AI is like calling a friend and asking for advice. Structured output is like giving them a form to fill out: "name, date, amount, address." The form always has the same fields in the same places — your software knows exactly where to look. Which would you rather process 10,000 of?

bangla.html: মডেলের মুক্ত-ভঙ্গির লেখাকে টাইপ-করা schema-তে বাধ্য করলে LLM বড় সিস্টেমের নির্ভরযোগ্য অংশ হয়ে ওঠে। এর তিনটি ক্রমশ কড়া স্তর আছে: JSON mode, schema-constrained decoding এবং typed parsing। প্রতিটি স্তরে নিশ্চয়তা ও নির্ভরযোগ্যতা বাড়ে।

Schema-constrained generation কীভাবে কাজ করে: প্রোভাইডার JSON schema-কে একটি finite-state machine (বা grammar)-এ রূপ দেয়, এবং প্রতিটি ধাপে যে token schema ভাঙবে তার logit mask করে দেয়। ফলে আউটপুট নির্মাণগতভাবেই parse-যোগ্য, আলাদা try/except দরকার হয় না।
Python-এ সাধারণত Pydantic মডেল (যেমন Person ক্লাসে name, age, role) বানিয়ে response_format=Person দিলে ফলাফল টাইপসহ parsed অবজেক্ট হিসেবে পাওয়া যায়। এতে regex, eval বা retry loop লাগে না।
সুতরাং সম্ভব হলেই structured outputs ব্যবহার করুন। FSM lookup-এর জন্য সামান্য latency বাড়ে, কিন্তু পরে validation-এর ঝামেলা বাঁচায় বলে সেটা সহজেই পুষিয়ে যায়।

blocks.html: সরকারি ফর্মের উপমা: কাউকে মুখে বললে সে নিজের মতো করে লম্বা গল্প শোনাবে। কিন্তু ব্যাংকের ফর্ম দিলে নাম, তারিখ, টাকার অঙ্ক নির্দিষ্ট ঘরেই লিখতে হয়। কেরানি তখন ঠিক জানে কোন তথ্য কোথায় পাবে। দশ হাজার ফর্ম প্রসেস করতে হলে কোনটা বেছে নেবেন?

practice.title: Compare loose and strict JSON output
practice.goal: See that a clear schema in the prompt gives cleaner, typed output than a loose request, and why prompts alone give no guarantee.
steps: Send Prompt A in a new chat. Look at the output: is it clean JSON that a program could parse?
Send Prompt B in another new chat. Compare the format, the types, and the missing age.
Paste each output into a free online JSON validator, or check by eye: only double quotes, no text outside the JSON.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
Put the people from this note into JSON.

Note: Hi team, please welcome Rahim Uddin, who joined us last week as our new data engineer. He is thirty-four. Also, Sadia Akter (QA lead) starts on Monday. I do not have her age yet.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
Extract the people from the note. Reply with JSON only. No text before or after it. No markdown code fence.

The JSON must be an array. Each item must follow this schema:
{"name": string, "age": integer or null, "role": string}
Use a number for age, not words. Use null if the age is not in the note. Do not add any other fields.

Note: Hi team, please welcome Rahim Uddin, who joined us last week as our new data engineer. He is thirty-four. Also, Sadia Akter (QA lead) starts on Monday. I do not have her age yet.

lookFor: Prompt A often adds a sentence before the JSON, uses a code fence, or invents its own field names.
Prompt B usually gives age 34 as a number and age null for Sadia. Prompt A might write 'thirty-four' or guess an age.
Even a good Prompt B result is only likely to be valid. Nothing in the chat forces it.

check.question: How is schema-constrained generation different from asking for JSON in a prompt?
check.answer: A prompt only asks the model to follow the format, so it can still fail. With schema-constrained generation the provider compiles the schema into a grammar and masks every token that would break it, so the output is parseable by construction.

practice.challenge: Add a third person with a role the schema does not expect, such as two roles. Ask the model to follow the schema and see how it handles the conflict.

sections.title: Function calling & tool use
sections.sub: Function calling lets the model emit a structured request to invoke a tool (a function, an API, a database query) instead of free-form prose. The model doesn't execute — it decides what to call and with what arguments, and your code runs the tool and feeds the result back. This is the basis of every LLM agent.

body.html: How it works under the hood

You supply a list of tools as JSON Schema (function name, parameters, description). The model is fine-tuned to emit a special tool_calls field instead of (or alongside) prose. Because the schema is constrained, the arguments are valid by construction. The leading paper is Toolformer (Meta, 2023),[18] with concurrent industry work on Gorilla (Berkeley, 2023) for massive API use,[17] and Anthropic's tool use docs.[27]

# Anthropic tool-use example
tools = [{
    "name": "get_weather",
    "description": "Get the current weather for a location.",
    "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["location"]
    }
}]

msg = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-5", tools=tools,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Dhaka?"}],
)
if msg.stop_reason == "tool_use":
    tool = msg.content[1]                    # tool-use block
    result = get_weather(**tool.input)          # your code
    # feed result back, model produces final answer

blocks.html: Tool design matters as much as model choice. Tool names and descriptions are inserted verbatim into the prompt. "Retrieve flights" is ambiguous; search_flights(origin, destination, depart_date, cabin_class) with documented parameters in the description yields dramatically higher correct-call rates. Iterate on tool descriptions the same way you iterate on prompts.

body.html: Modern patterns

items: Parallel tool calls: OpenAI's tool_choice: "auto" can emit multiple independent calls per turn — the model decides what can run concurrently.
Chain-of-Abstraction: the model writes placeholders for tool results, then fills them in after parallel execution — saves wall time on multi-step agents.[19]
Computer use: Sonnet 4.5 and similar can drive a desktop via screenshot + mouse/keyboard primitives — the "ultimate tool" with the agent acting as the API.

layman.html: Tools turn an LLM from a brain in a jar into something that can actually do things. Without tools, the AI can only write essays. With tools, it can look up your calendar, query Wikipedia, run a database search, send an email, book a flight, or even drive your computer mouse.

How does it work? You tell the AI what tools are available, like giving a new assistant a keyring: get_weather(city), send_email(to, subject, body), search_database(query). The AI reads your question, decides which tool(s) to use, and writes a structured request like {"tool": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Dhaka"}}. Your software runs that tool — the AI itself can't touch anything. Then it gets the result and writes the final answer.
This is the heart of every "AI agent." ChatGPT that browses the web for you? Tool. Cursor that edits your code? Tool. The AI that books your appointments? Tool.
The loop repeats: AI thinks → calls tool → reads result → calls next tool → ... → eventually writes the final reply. The smarter the AI, the more steps it can chain before getting confused.

The catch: the more tools you give, the harder the AI has to think about which one to use. Too many tools = bad choices. Good tool design (clear names, descriptions, parameter docs) matters as much as the model choice.

blocks.html: The sous chef analogy: the AI is a brilliant chef who can't leave the kitchen. You stock the kitchen with tools: a stove, a blender, a knife. The chef can use any of them to make dinner, but YOU had to buy them and put them there. If you stock the kitchen with 200 weird gadgets, the chef gets confused. Stock it with the 10 right tools and magic happens.

bangla.html: Function calling মানে মডেল সরাসরি কিছু চালায় না; বরং কোন tool (ফাংশন, API, ডেটাবেস কোয়েরি) কোন argument দিয়ে ডাকতে হবে তা একটি structured অনুরোধ হিসেবে বের করে দেয়। আপনার কোড tool চালায় এবং ফলাফল মডেলকে ফেরত দেয়। প্রতিটি LLM agent এই ধারণার ওপর দাঁড়িয়ে।

লুপটি ReAct-ধাঁচের: মডেল tool-call JSON দেয়, কোড সেটি চালায়, ফলাফল কনভারসেশনে যোগ হয়, আর এভাবে চলতে থাকে। আপনি tool-এর তালিকা JSON Schema আকারে দেন (নাম, parameters, description), এবং মডেল prose-এর বদলে (বা সাথে) tool_calls ফিল্ড বের করতে fine-tuned। Schema constrained বলে arguments বৈধ হয়। Anthropic-এ stop_reason == "tool_use" হলে tool-use block থেকে input নিয়ে নিজের ফাংশন চালাতে হয়।

Tool design মডেল বাছাইয়ের মতোই গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। Tool-এর নাম ও description হুবহু prompt-এ ঢোকে। "Retrieve flights" অস্পষ্ট; কিন্তু search_flights(origin, destination, depart_date, cabin_class) এবং description-এ প্রতিটি parameter-এর ব্যাখ্যা থাকলে সঠিক কলের হার অনেক বাড়ে। Prompt-এর মতোই tool description বারবার উন্নত করুন।

items: Parallel tool calls: একাধিক স্বাধীন কল এক turn-এ দেওয়া যায়।
Chain-of-Abstraction: মডেল ফলাফলের placeholder লিখে রাখে, পরে সমান্তরালে চালিয়ে পূরণ করা হয়, ফলে multi-step agent-এর সময় বাঁচে।
Computer use: screenshot ও mouse/keyboard দিয়ে ডেস্কটপ চালানো, যেন agent নিজেই API।

blocks.html: ম্যানেজার ও অফিস সহকারীর উপমা: ম্যানেজার (মডেল) নিজে ফাইল আনতে বা ফোন করতে যায় না। সে লিখে দেয়, "রহিমকে ফোন করে আজকের বিক্রি জানাও।" সহকারী (আপনার কোড) কাজটি করে ফলাফল ফেরত দেয়, তারপর ম্যানেজার সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়। সহকারীর হাতে কাজের তালিকা যত স্পষ্ট, ভুল তত কম।

practice.goal: Do the tool loop by hand: the model asks for a tool call, you run the tool, and the model uses your result.

prompts.text:
You can use these tools. You cannot run them yourself. To use a tool, reply with ONLY a JSON object: {"tool": name, "arguments": {...}}. No other text.

Tools:
[
  {"name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather for a city.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"]}}, "required": ["location"]}},

]

lookFor: The first reply is only a JSON call to get_weather with location Dhaka. It is not an answer, and the model did not look up any weather.
The final answer uses your fake 38 degrees. The model trusts the tool result you gave it.
The model chose get_weather and not search_flights. The tool names and descriptions guided the choice.

check.question: In function calling, who runs the tool: the model or your code?
check.answer: Your code runs the tool. The model only decides which tool to call and with what arguments, then reads the result you append to the conversation. This loop of call, run, append, repeat is the base of every LLM agent.

body.captionBn: এখানে দেখা যায় image, audio waveform ও PDF / doc page প্রতিটি আলাদা encoder দিয়ে প্রক্রিয়া হয়। এরপর projection দিয়ে token sequence-এ রূপান্তরিত হয়ে text tokens-এর সাথে concat হয় এবং LLM core-এর joint attention সবগুলোকে একসাথে প্রক্রিয়া করে।

body.html: Capability comparison (2025)

rows: Most natively multimodal[10][11][12]

blocks.html: Vision is not magic OCR. Frontier vision LLMs can count, read handwriting, reason about charts, and even interpret UI screenshots — but they still hallucinate on tiny text, fine numerics, and rotated pages. For high-precision OCR (invoices, IDs, scientific notation), use a dedicated OCR engine and feed the text to a text LLM.

body.html: PDFs are a special case

Frontier APIs accept PDFs directly (Claude, Gemini) and render each page as an image. The alternatives:
• Text-extract first: pymupdf, pdfplumber, unstructured.io — fast, cheap, but loses layout & visuals.
• Vision path: render pages → multimodal LLM — slower, expensive, but handles scanned docs, tables, charts.
• Hybrid: text-extract + page-image for tables/figures. This is what production systems ship.

layman.html: Modern AI isn't just text anymore. You can paste a photo of a handwritten note, a chart, an X-ray, a screenshot, a 200-page PDF, or even a 30-second voice clip — and the AI can read, describe, and reason about it like a human would.
How? Each input type is first run through a specialist mini-model:

• Images get chopped into patches; a vision model (like CLIP) describes each patch as numbers.
• Audio gets converted into a spectrogram; a speech model transcribes it.
• PDFs get split into pages; some pages become text (extractable), others become images (scanned).
All these numbers then get poured into the same LLM as if they were extra "words." The AI doesn't think in pixels or sound — it thinks in numbers that represent pixels or sound.

What can it actually do? Read a graph. Count objects in a photo. Read a screenshot and click the right button. Look at a form photo and output the form data as JSON. Watch a video and summarise it. Listen to a lecture and take notes. (Some of these still hallucinate — see the warning below.)

Caution: AI vision is impressive but still imperfect on tiny text (receipts, IDs), precise numbers, rotated pages, and unfamiliar scripts. For high-precision OCR, use a dedicated OCR engine (Tesseract, Google Document AI) and feed the text to the LLM.

blocks.html: The translator analogy: imagine you're a brilliant lawyer who only speaks English. You have a team of translators: one for Chinese, one for photos, one for music. They each convert their specialty into English notes you can read. You don't see the original — but you understand the meaning well enough to give legal advice.

bangla.html: আধুনিক ফ্রন্টিয়ার মডেল শুধু টেক্সট নয়, ছবি, অডিও, ভিডিও ফ্রেম ও PDF পৃষ্ঠাও নেয়। মূল কৌশল: যেকোনো modality-কে embedding vector-এর ক্রমে রূপ দিয়ে টেক্সটের ক্রমের সাথে জুড়ে দেওয়া হয়। প্রতিটি modality-র নিজস্ব encoder থাকে, একটি শেখা projection সেগুলোকে LLM-এর token space-এ নিয়ে আসে, আর একটিই transformer সবকিছুর ওপর attention দেয়।

ক্ষমতা মডেলভেদে আলাদা: Gemini 1.5/2.5 সবচেয়ে native multimodal (ছবি, অডিও in/out, ভিডিও, PDF); GPT-4o ছবিতে ভালো; Claude 4 চার্ট ও ডায়াগ্রাম পড়ায় ভালো; Qwen-VL ও Llama 3.2 Vision হলো open-weight vision মডেল।

সতর্কতা: Vision মানেই নিখুঁত OCR নয়। মডেল গুনতে, হাতের লেখা পড়তে, চার্ট বুঝতে পারে, কিন্তু ছোট লেখা, সূক্ষ্ম সংখ্যা ও ঘোরানো পৃষ্ঠায় hallucinate করে। ইনভয়েস, ID বা বৈজ্ঞানিক নোটেশনের মতো নিখুঁত দরকারে আলাদা OCR engine ব্যবহার করে টেক্সটটি text LLM-কে দিন।
PDF-এর তিনটি পথ:

items: Text-extract আগে (pymupdf, pdfplumber, unstructured.io): দ্রুত ও সস্তা, কিন্তু layout ও ভিজ্যুয়াল হারায়।
Vision path (পৃষ্ঠা render করে multimodal LLM-এ): ধীর ও ব্যয়বহুল, কিন্তু scanned ডকুমেন্ট, টেবিল ও চার্ট সামলায়।
Hybrid: টেক্সট extract এবং টেবিল/ফিগারের জন্য পৃষ্ঠার ছবি। প্রোডাকশনে এটিই বেশি চলে।

blocks.html: বহুভাষী দোভাষী দলের উপমা: একজন বিচারক শুধু বাংলা জানেন। তাঁর সাথে আছে একজন চীনা দোভাষী, একজন ছবির বিশ্লেষক ও একজন অডিও লিপিকার। প্রত্যেকে নিজের বিষয় বাংলা নোটে বদলে দেয়, আর বিচারক সেই নোট পড়েই রায় দেন। তিনি আসল জিনিস দেখেন না, কিন্তু অর্থ ঠিকই বোঝেন।

practice.title: Test vision on sharp and tiny text
practice.goal: See that a vision model can read a clear table, but makes mistakes on tiny text, so it is not a perfect OCR engine.
steps: Open the capability comparison table in this section. Take a screenshot of it at normal size. Use only the table, with no private data.
Send the screenshot with Prompt A in a new chat. Your chat must allow image upload.
Zoom your browser out to about 30%. Take a new screenshot of the same table. Send it with Prompt A in another new chat.
Compare the two copies against the real table. Count the mistakes.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text: Look at the attached image. Copy the table into text, one row per line, with the exact words and symbols. After the copy, list every cell where you are not sure of the text.

lookFor: The clear screenshot is usually copied well, with few or no mistakes.
The tiny screenshot often has missing rows, wrong words, or guessed cells.
Models often write the guessed text with the same confidence as the correct text, unless you ask which cells are unsure.

check.question: Why does the model get worse when the text in the image is tiny?
check.answer: An image is encoded into a sequence of embedding vectors that the transformer reads like tokens. Tiny text has too little detail in those vectors, so the model guesses. For exact text such as invoices or IDs, a dedicated OCR engine is more reliable.

practice.challenge: Take a photo of a short handwritten note, or write one on paper. Send it with Prompt A and check which words the model reads wrong.

sections.title: Embedding models & reranker models
sections.sub: Two specialised model types that, together with an LLM, form the standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) stack. Embeddings compress text into a vector such that semantically similar items land near each other. Rerankers score (query, document) pairs with cross-attention for higher precision.

body.html: Embedding models (bi-encoders)

Encode each side (query and document) independently into a fixed-size vector. Similarity is a dot product or cosine — O(1) per pair, allowing billion-scale ANN search with FAISS, ScaNN, or HNSW. Modern examples: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, Cohere embed-v3, BGE-M3, E5-Mistral-7B.[21]

Reranker models (cross-encoders)

Rerankers concatenate query + document and run full transformer attention across them — much more accurate but O(n) per pair. Best used as the second stage on top-K=100 candidates.[22] Recent papers show LLM-based rerankers (even small open ones like Qwen2.5-7B) can match proprietary rerankers with listwise ranking prompts.

rows: Encode once, search billions in ms

blocks.html: The state-of-the-art 2025 stack: embed with E5-Mistral-7B-instruct or BGE-M3 for open weights, rerank with Qwen3-Reranker or Cohere Rerank v3, generate with your favourite LLM. Hybrid retrieval (sparse BM25 + dense) consistently beats either alone on BEIR.

layman.html: How does an AI know what's in your 10,000-doc knowledge base without reading all of it? Two specialised models: one fast-and-loose, one slow-and-precise.

Embeddings: a fancy index. Imagine every document in your library gets summarised into a list of numbers — say 1,000 numbers — that captures its meaning. Similar documents get similar numbers. Now you can search by meaning: "find me stuff related to climate insurance" finds documents that mean similar things, even if they don't share any words. The trick is: you can compare 1,000 numbers against a million other documents in milliseconds. That's how ChatGPT's "Search" can scan your entire Drive in seconds.

Rerankers: the tiebreaker. Embeddings are fast but sloppy. Sometimes the top 10 "most similar" documents aren't really the best 10. A reranker takes that shortlist and reads each one against your question, like a careful human librarian deciding which book is truly the best answer. Slow, but accurate.
The two-stage pipeline:

1. Embedding model narrows 10 million docs → 100 likely candidates (in 50ms).
2. Reranker picks the best 5 from those 100 (in another 200ms).
3. The LLM reads those 5 and writes the final answer.
This is what powers every "ChatGPT, search my docs" feature, every customer-support bot that knows your product manual, every legal-AI tool that scans case law.

blocks.html: The librarian analogy: embeddings are a librarian who skims the back cover of every book in milliseconds and grabs the 100 that look promising. Reranking is the senior librarian who reads those 100 covers more carefully and picks the 3 winners. The LLM is you, reading those 3 winners and writing the answer.

bangla.html: RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) স্ট্যাকে LLM-এর সাথে দুই ধরনের বিশেষায়িত মডেল থাকে। Embedding model টেক্সটকে এমন একটি vector-এ সংকুচিত করে যাতে সমার্থক জিনিস কাছাকাছি পড়ে। Reranker (query, document) জোড়াকে cross-attention দিয়ে স্কোর করে বেশি নিখুঁত ফল দেয়।

Embedding (bi-encoder): query ও document আলাদা আলাদা করে নির্দিষ্ট আকারের vector বানানো হয়। সাদৃশ্য মাপা হয় dot product বা cosine দিয়ে, প্রতি জোড়ায় O(1), তাই FAISS, ScaNN বা HNSW দিয়ে বিলিয়ন-স্কেল ANN সার্চ সম্ভব। উদাহরণ: text-embedding-3-large, embed-v3, BGE-M3, E5-Mistral-7B।

Reranker (cross-encoder): query ও document জুড়ে পুরো transformer attention চালায়। অনেক নিখুঁত, কিন্তু প্রতি জোড়ায় O(n) এবং প্রায় 50–200 ms, তাই এটি দ্বিতীয় ধাপে, শীর্ষ প্রায় 100 candidate-এর ওপর ব্যবহার করা উচিত।

items: Stage 1 (bi-encoder): একবার encode করে মিলিসেকেন্ডে কোটি কোটির মধ্যে খোঁজা; recall ভালো, precision কম।
Stage 2 (cross-encoder): কোনো vector সংরক্ষণ নেই, টেক্সটের ওপর চলে; precision সেরা।

bangla.html: 2025-এর আধুনিক স্ট্যাক: open-weight-এ E5-Mistral-7B-instruct বা BGE-M3 দিয়ে embed, Qwen3-Reranker বা Cohere Rerank v3 দিয়ে rerank, তারপর পছন্দের LLM দিয়ে উত্তর তৈরি। Hybrid retrieval (sparse BM25 + dense) BEIR-এ প্রায় সবসময় একা কোনোটির চেয়ে ভালো ফল দেয়।

blocks.html: চাকরির নিয়োগের উপমা: হাজার হাজার সিভি এলে প্রথমে একটি কম্পিউটার কিওয়ার্ড মিলিয়ে ঝটপট একশোটি বেছে নেয় (embedding)। তারপর অভিজ্ঞ HR ম্যানেজার সেই একশোটি মন দিয়ে পড়ে সেরা কয়েকজনকে ইন্টারভিউয়ের জন্য ডাকেন (reranker)। শেষে সিদ্ধান্ত নেন বস (LLM)।

practice.title: Judge meaning, not matching words
practice.goal: See that similarity depends on meaning, not shared words, and that a second step that reads query and document together picks better answers.
steps: Send Prompt A in a new chat. Look at the scores for each pair.
Send Prompt B in the same chat. Look at which documents get the top scores.
Find a document that shares many words with the query but scores low. Say why.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text:
Rate how similar the meaning of each pair is, from 0 (unrelated) to 1 (same meaning). Reply with one line per pair: the pair number and the score only.

1. 'How do I reset my password?' / 'Steps to recover access to my account when I forgot my login secret'
2. 'The bank was flooded after heavy rain.' / 'I deposited money at the bank this morning.'
3. 'How do I reset my password?' / 'How do I reset my router?'
4. 'How do I reset my password?' / 'Best street food in Old Dhaka'

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text:
Query: Can I return a laptop after 40 days?

Documents:
D1: Laptops can be returned within 14 days of delivery if the box is unopened.
D2: Laptop deals: save 20% on laptops this week, with free delivery on every laptop.
D3: Standard items can be returned within 30 days. Electronics have a shorter window.
D4: How to pack a laptop for a return shipment: use the original box and two layers of tape.
D5: Every laptop has a 12 month warranty. Defective laptops can be repaired or replaced at any time in that period.

Score each document from 0 to 10 for how well it helps answer the query. Then list the documents from best to worst. Give one short reason for each.

lookFor: Pair 1 gets a high score even with few shared words. Pairs 2 and 3 get low scores even with shared words.
Pair 4 gets a score near 0.
D2 and D4 repeat the word laptop many times, but they usually score low. D1 and D3 usually rank highest, because they answer the return question.

check.question: Why do an embedding model and a reranker form a two-stage pipeline?
check.answer: A bi-encoder embeds each text alone, so it can search millions of vectors fast, but its precision is lower. A cross-encoder reranker reads the query and document together, which is more accurate but slow, so it re-scores only the top candidates.

practice.challenge: Add a document D6 that answers the question perfectly but uses very different words, such as Items bought online may be sent back for a refund up to two weeks after arrival. Where does it rank?

body.captionBn: এখানে Standard মডেল ও Reasoning মডেলের পার্থক্য দেখানো হয়েছে। Standard-এ user prompt থেকে সরাসরি one shot answer আসে; Reasoning মডেলে answer-এর আগে অনেক thinking tokens ("Let's think step by step…") খরচ হয়, তারপর final answer আসে।

body.html: The training trick: RL on reasoning chains

OpenAI's o1 paper showed that reinforcement learning on chain-of-thought traces dramatically improves math/physics/code reasoning — the model learns to think longer on hard problems.[13] DeepSeek-R1 replicated this with pure RL (no SFT), open-weights.[7] Anthropic's "extended thinking" exposes this as a togglable parameter.[28]
When extended thinking helps
Engineering trade-offs

blocks.html: Reasoning models can use 5–50× more tokens per query. A "thinking budget" cap is essential — set it to your latency/cost ceiling.
TTFT is often slower (longer prefill). Streaming the thinking tokens can help UX.
DeepSeek-R1 distilled into Qwen 1.5B–32B gives small open models with reasoning capabilities.[7]
"Let's verify step by step" showed step-level reward models beat outcome-only supervision on math.[24]

body.html:
# Anthropic extended thinking
resp = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
    thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 10000},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Prove sqrt(2) is irrational"}],
)
for block in resp.content:
    if block.type == "thinking":  print("…", block.thinking)
    if block.type == "text":      print(block.text)

blocks.html: Don't reach for reasoning models by reflex. They're 5–50× more expensive and slower. Use them when (1) the task is math/code/agentic, (2) standard models have plateaued on your benchmark, and (3) you can afford the latency. For most chat / extraction / RAG, a standard model + careful prompting wins.

body.html: The frontier as of Q3 2025

items: Reasoning models are the default for hard tasks: GPT-5, o3, DeepSeek-R1, Claude 4 with extended thinking.[13][7]
Open-weight models match closed on many benchmarks (Qwen3, Llama 3.1 405B, DeepSeek-V3).[9][3][6]
Multimodal is now table stakes: Gemini 2.5, GPT-4o, Claude 4, Qwen3-VL all native.[12]
Long context (1M+) is real but doesn't replace good retrieval.
Tool-use agents are the dominant deployment pattern.

layman.html: Sometimes the AI needs to "think before it speaks." A regular AI answers instantly: you ask "What's 17 × 24?" and it blurts an answer (maybe wrong). A reasoning AI scribbles for 30 seconds first — breaking the problem into pieces, checking its work, considering alternatives — then gives you the answer.
Think of it like two students taking an exam.

• Standard AI = the kid who writes the first thing that pops into their head. Fast, sometimes brilliant, often sloppy.
• Reasoning AI = the kid who works through the problem on scratch paper, tries two methods, checks the answer. Slow, almost always right on hard stuff.

Where reasoning models win dramatically: math, logic, multi-step coding, planning complex tasks, scientific questions. OpenAI's o1/o3, Claude with "extended thinking," DeepSeek-R1 — these all spend 5–50× more "thinking time" than regular models, and the quality jump is real.
Where they're a waste: "Write me a thank-you email." "Summarise this article." "Translate this sentence." You'd be paying 50× more for the same answer. Use the regular model for everyday stuff.

The catch: reasoning models cost a lot. They're 5–50× more expensive per query, and they take longer. So pick them deliberately, like calling a math tutor for the hard homework but doing the easy drills yourself.

The cool part: you can limit the "thinking budget." Tell Claude "spend up to 5,000 tokens thinking, then answer." For easy questions it finishes early. For hard ones, it uses the full budget. You control the speed/quality dial.

blocks.html: The patient friend analogy: regular AI = your friend who blurts answers quickly. Reasoning AI = your friend who pauses, says "let me think about this," scribbles for a minute, then gives you a careful answer. You go to the patient friend for the important questions; the quick friend is fine for casual stuff.

bangla.html: Reasoning model এমন একটি নতুন শ্রেণির মডেল যা কঠিন সমস্যায় inference-এর সময় বেশি compute খরচ করে। সরাসরি উত্তর না দিয়ে প্রথমে অভ্যন্তরীণ chain of reasoning ("thinking tokens") লেখে, তারপর চূড়ান্ত উত্তর দেয়। GPT-4-এর পর এটিকেই সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ সক্ষমতার পরিবর্তন বলা হচ্ছে।

প্রশিক্ষণের কৌশল: chain-of-thought-এর ওপর reinforcement learning (RL) প্রয়োগ করলে math, physics ও code reasoning অনেক ভালো হয়, কারণ মডেল কঠিন সমস্যায় বেশি ভাবতে শেখে। OpenAI-এর o1 এটি দেখিয়েছে; DeepSeek-R1 শুধু RL দিয়ে (SFT ছাড়া) open-weight আকারে তা পুনরায় করেছে; আর Anthropic-এ extended thinking একটি চালু/বন্ধ করার parameter। Process reward model-ও step-level পুরস্কার দিয়ে math-এ outcome-only supervision-কে ছাড়িয়ে গেছে।

items: কখন কাজে লাগে: math/physics/proof, কঠিন multi-step কোডিং agent, planning ও tool orchestration।
কখন অপচয়: chat, summarisation, extraction, সহজ Q&A ও classification; এসবে ছোট/দ্রুত মডেলই ভালো।

bangla.html: Engineering trade-off: প্রতি query-তে 5–50 গুণ বেশি token লাগতে পারে, তাই latency/খরচের সীমা অনুযায়ী budget_tokens (thinking budget) সীমা দেওয়া জরুরি। Prefill লম্বা হওয়ায় TTFT প্রায়ই ধীর হয়; thinking token stream করলে UX ভালো হয়। Distillation-এর মাধ্যমে R1-এর ক্ষমতা Qwen 1.5B–32B-এর মতো ছোট open মডেলে আনা গেছে।

অভ্যাসবশে reasoning মডেল নেবেন না। ব্যবহার করুন যখন (১) কাজটি math/code/agentic, (২) সাধারণ মডেল আপনার benchmark-এ আর এগোচ্ছে না, এবং (৩) latency সহ্য করা যায়। বেশিরভাগ chat/extraction/RAG-এ সাধারণ মডেল ও ভালো prompting-ই যথেষ্ট।

blocks.html: গণিত পরীক্ষার উপমা: সহজ অঙ্ক পরীক্ষার হলে অনেকে মুখে মুখে করে ফেলে। কিন্তু কঠিন জ্যামিতি বা বীজগণিতে ভালো ছাত্র খাতায় ধাপে ধাপে লেখে, নিজের উত্তর মিলিয়ে দেখে। এতে সময় বেশি লাগে, কিন্তু উত্তর ঠিক হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা বাড়ে। সব প্রশ্নে এত সময় দেওয়াও বোকামি।

practice.title: Compare quick answers with step-by-step thinking
practice.goal: See that thinking steps help on multi-step problems, and that on easy questions they only add length and cost.
steps: Send Prompt A in a new chat. Note the number. Work the correct answer out yourself with a calculator.
Send Prompt B in another new chat. Compare the result, and the length of the answer.
Send Prompt C in a new chat. Compare its length with a plain question and answer.

prompts.label: Prompt A
prompts.text: A bakery bakes 8 trays with 25 buns each. 12% of all buns are burnt and thrown away. The rest are sold in full boxes of 6 buns at $4.50 per box. Buns that do not fill a box are given away free. How much money does the bakery earn? Reply with the final amount only. Do not show any working.

prompts.label: Prompt B
prompts.text: A bakery bakes 8 trays with 25 buns each. 12% of all buns are burnt and thrown away. The rest are sold in full boxes of 6 buns at $4.50 per box. Buns that do not fill a box are given away free. How much money does the bakery earn? Think step by step. Then give the final line as: Answer: $amount

prompts.label: Prompt C
prompts.text: Think step by step, then answer: What is the capital of Japan?

lookFor: The correct answer is $130.50. Many modern models get it right even in Prompt A, but fast answers fail more often on multi-step problems.
Prompt B shows each step: 200 buns, 24 burnt, 176 left, 29 full boxes, then the money. This makes errors easy to see.
Prompt C gives a long answer to a one-word question. This is the waste that reasoning adds on easy tasks.

check.question: Why do reasoning models use 5 to 50 times more tokens, and when is it worth it?
check.answer: They spend extra compute at inference time by writing thinking tokens before the final answer. This helps on hard math, code, and planning tasks, but it adds cost and latency, so for simple chat or extraction a standard model is better.

practice.challenge: If your chat has a Think or Reasoning mode, turn it on and send Prompt A again. Does the answer change, and does the response take longer?
